title: Palisades (Holtec restart): Palisades - Request for Additional Information Re: DD41 Exigent Amendment [['E-Mail', 'Request for Additional Information (RAI)']]

documents.text:
Brent Ballard

From:                            Brent Ballard
Sent:                            Wednesday, October 7, 2026 1:31 PM
To:                              ext_KYLE_STEFFIC; 'Kami Miller'
Cc:                              Justin Poole; Marlayna Doell
Subject:                         RE: Palisades - Request for Additional Information DD41


Hi Kyle,

Apologize, but there is a second part to question 1, related to operation of the crane as it related to a cask drop
accident. I’m restating the complete questions below and the new text is highlighted:

    1. Is there an analysis of a cask drop over the spent fuel pool? If so, does the cask drop over the spent fuel
       pool bound a drop of DD41 (in the FTC) onto the fuel. Please supplement the LAR to include a section
       discussing how a hypothetical drop of the Fuel Transfer Canister onto spent fuel in the spent fuel pool is
       bounded by existing analysis. Section 9.11.4.3 (Item 6) of the FSAR indicates, “The Fuel Building Crane may
       be operated in a non-single failure proof manner following site-speciﬁc heavy load requirements. Non-
       single failure proof modes of operation typically involve trolley and bridge speed increases and multiple
       direction movement control, and are only used when single failure proof operation is not required. Section
       14.11 describes postulated cask drop accidents.” Section 14.11.1 of FSAR indicates “In these situations,
       the crane no longer meets single failure proof requirements, and load drops are postulated.” Since fuel
       transfer canister will be travelling over spent fuel within the fuel building and load drop analysis has not
       been performed, conﬁrm FB crane is operated in single failure proof manner. In event the crane is not
       handled in single failure proof manner, is an impact limiting pad required as indicated in Section
       14.11.2.3.1 of FSAR?

    2. NRC sta understands that fuel assembly DD41 exhibits signiﬁcant bowing. Based on the fuel transfer
       canister (FTC) drawings made available on the portal, it does not appear that the FTC design
       accommodates this degree of bowing. Once DD41 is placed in the FTC, will measurements be taken to
       conﬁrm the actual extent of bowing? The sta ’s concern is that when the FTC lid is installed, any existing
       bowing will be essentially forced into a straighter conﬁguration, which could result in additional damage to
       the assembly and/or fuel rods. Please describe what evaluations or controls have been implemented to
       ensure that no further damage will occur when DD41 is enclosed in the FTC. Additionally, are contingency
       actions established in the event that the assembly is adversely a ected when the FTC lid is secured?

Thanks,
Brent

Hi Kyle,

Please see below for two additional requests for additional information. These are more involved than RCIs and
will require response. One is an outcome of us now understanding you do intend to move the loaded FTC over
spent fuel. The other relates to bowing of the assembly and how that may impact loading in the FTC:

As of now, I think we were able to internally resolve the RCIs I mentioned but we may still have some before we
wrap this up. I didn’t want to hold up on the RAIs since the response will be more involved. Please let me know if
you want to discuss either of these with the sta .

Thanks,
Brent
